title: Using Motif Transitions for Temporal Graph Generation

problem.claim: Temporal graph generators are needed to produce realistic synthetic temporal networks for surrogate data sharing and benchmarking.

gap.claim: Existing temporal network generation models are often restricted to a small set of predefined temporal motif patterns because counting temporal motifs is computationally costly.

contributions.claim: The work develops a practical temporal graph generator called the Motif Transition Model (MTM) for generating synthetic temporal networks with realistic global and local features.
MTM models the arrival of new events as temporal motif transition processes.
The method calculates transition properties from an input graph and simulates motif transition processes using transition probabilities and transition rates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MTM consistently outperforms baselines in preserving various global and local temporal graph statistics and in runtime performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph generative models support surrogate data sharing and benchmarking, while real-world systems often evolve as temporal networks.
Existing temporal network generators extend static graph generators with temporal processes, and temporal motifs have recently been used with improved results.
Many existing models remain limited to a small set of predefined motif patterns because temporal motif counting is computationally expensive.
MTM generates synthetic temporal networks by modeling new-event arrivals as motif transitions and simulating them from learned transition properties, probabilities, and rates.
The authors report better preservation of global and local temporal graph statistics and better runtime performance than baselines.

source_observation.claim: Modeling new-event arrivals as temporal motif transition processes is used to generate synthetic temporal networks.

interpretation.claim: Representing temporal evolution through transitions between recurring local structures may help capture both local and global network behavior.

application.claim: Consider transition-based temporal motif models when building generators for surrogate data or temporal graph benchmarks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance outside the reported temporal graph generation setting or specify which motif patterns and statistics are covered.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the transition-property estimation procedure in detail.
The abstract does not report scalability limits or the computational cost of MTM.
